messages:
Maya Patel: Quick one  bought a prepaid SIM and 5GB top-up at AMS for a 5-day customer trip, total 45. Used about 2 days for customer calls. Receipt attached. Do I expense full amount or split? Any airport telecom rules?

Juan (People Ops): Reimbursable if business-critical. Short: claim business portion and attach the itemized receipt + manager approval.

Maya Patel: Sweet. Do I need preapproval retroactively? Didnt think to ask before buying.

Juan (People Ops): No retro approval needed for small buys. If > 75 get manager or #people-ops sign-off. Code to `mobile-internet`.

Oliver Kim: I can approve the work portion. @Maya confirm how many days were work-related and add note. :thumbsup: 

Maya Patel: Thanks Oliver. Should I pro-rate by days or data used?

Elena (Accounting): Days-based pro-rate is preferred (privacy). So 2/5 = 40% business. Claim 40% of 45 = 18. Include note: "2/5 days business f approved by Oliver Kim" and attach receipt.

Finance Bot: Upload original itemized receipt (photo/pdf). If card charge in non-EUR we'll use the card rate; cash uses exchange rate on expense date.

Juan (People Ops): A few quick policy points:
- Airport kiosk receipts must be itemized (SIM/data). Generic slip may be rejected.
- Purchases including devices or hardware > 150 need preapproval and asset tagging.
- For mixed personal/business, include manager attestation in notes.

Maya Patel: Got the itemized receipt, paid cash. I'll submit with 40% and Oliver's note. Anything about VAT?

Elena (Accounting): We only reclaim VAT if vendor issues an invoice in company name. Kiosk sales rarely do. Submit normally; VAT won't be reclaimed.

Juan (People Ops): Policy snippet: telecom & mobile data reimbursable when needed for customer work, receipt required, pro-rate for personal use, preapproval > 75. Link: <https://redwood.company/policies/expenses#telecom>

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone f submitting now.

Oliver Kim: Approved.

Elena (Accounting): Received and processing at 40% non-VAT reclaimable. Will follow up if anything else needed.
